== Title ==
<span lang="ja">オゼル提督</span>. One asterisk precedes the printed title.<ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source" />

== Card Text ==
<span lang="ja">自分の大型艦は同じ星系に－1で配備できる。操縦する宇宙船の戦闘力に2を加える。場にベイダーが出ており、相手がオゼルと同じロケーションにリアクションで移動してきたなら、オゼル提督は即座にロストする。</span><ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source" />

== Lore ==
<span lang="ja">反乱軍を発見し壊滅させるために皇帝が編成したデス・スコードロンの<u>リーダー</u>。愚鈍で不器用。ダース・ベイダーに失策を露呈したばかりで、もはや失敗は許されない。</span><ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source" />

== Translation of Japanese Text ==
AI English reading aid (Memory Core ChatGPT, 7 November 2026).

'''Title'''
<blockquote>Admiral Ozzel</blockquote>

'''Lore'''
<blockquote>Leader of the Death Squadron formed by the Emperor to find and destroy the Rebels. Stupid and clumsy. Having just exposed his failure to Darth Vader, he can afford no further failures.</blockquote>

'''Game text'''
<blockquote>Your capital starships may deploy at -1 to the same system. Adds 2 to the power of the starship he pilots. If Vader is on the table and the opponent moves to Ozzel's location as a react, Admiral Ozzel is immediately lost.</blockquote>

The Japanese lore expresses the English “next-to-last time” joke as allowing no further failures. Its final game-text condition explicitly says that the opponent moves to Ozzel's location as a react (リアクションで移動してきた), where the original English says only that the opponent “‘reacts’ to same location as Ozzel.” Both original faces restrict his +2 pilot bonus to a starship.<ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source" /><ref name="english-face">[[:File:Hoth-D-admiralozzel-decipher-archive.gif|Original English card face]].</ref>

== Rules ==
The November 1998 [[Media:Decipher Glossary 1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] states that English is the standard for tournament play, directing foreign-language cards and rules to be played and interpreted as their English counterparts under current rulings, errata and clarifications.<ref name="foreign-language-rule">[[Media:Decipher Glossary 1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (November 1998), p. 62, Foreign-language cards and rules.</ref>
